title.en: Australia politics live: Coalition accuses Labor of treating veterans ‘with contempt’; Victorian Liberals pledge to ‘throw open doors to gas’
title.zh: 澳大利亚政治直播：联盟党指责工党“蔑视”退伍军人；维多利亚州自由党承诺“向天然气敞开大门”

summary.en: Australian political parties are engaged in accusations, with the Coalition alleging Labor treats veterans with contempt. Meanwhile, Victorian Liberals are proposing to expand gas access, and a politician has noted a collapse in housing market confidence due to rising rents.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚政党之间相互指责，联盟党指控工党“蔑视”退伍军人。与此同时，维多利亚州自由党承诺“向天然气敞开大门”，一位政治家指出，由于租金上涨，住房市场信心已“崩溃”。

body.en: Follow today’s news live Follow our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast ‘Collapsing confidence’ in housing market, Wilson says Tim Wilson has jumped on that reporting around rent increases and says there has been a collapse in confidence since the budget which is hurting renters. We’ve had, since the budget, collapsing confidence, a lack of will to invest in housing that is going to be available for rentals. We’re seeing a complete disaster in the housing market, and we know that’s only going to do one thing while the government continues to overshoot its migration target, and that is an increase in rents on Australians struggling to save a first home deposit. There is an awful lot that goes into determining rents in Australia, and the thing that Treasury modelled in the context of the budget, what is the isolated effect of what the government actually changed about the housing market. And if I just step back for a second, we’ve got a broken housing system in our country, and it’s the renters of Australia who are bearing the brunt of really 40 years of government’s not doing enough about this problem. I think that Clare sadly needs to start taking a bit of responsibility for her housing policy. But also, Clare, stop gaslighting Australians, stop gaslighting the mum and dads who are currently watching this show and feeling the impact of your toxic housing taxes … She can sit on your show and defend her policies, but the evidence on the ground, the evidence from the experts, is that Labor’s toxic housing taxes are smashing the market. title.en: Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for presidential election
title.zh: 被解雇的乌克兰国防部长呼吁举行总统选举

summary.en: Martial law has been in place in Ukraine since February 2022, under which elections are suspended.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for wartime elections, in what many see as the biggest challenge to Volodymyr Zelensky's presidency since war broke out with Russia in February 2022.

"Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia," said Fedorov, 35, in a video posted to YouTube on Tuesday, adding that Ukraine is fighting "precisely because we want to remain a free European state".

Since Russia's invasion Ukraine has been under martial law, which means elections are suspended.

Fedorov, who did not mention Zelensky by name in the video, was unexpectedly fired from his role as defence minister in late July, just six months after his appointment.

Zelensky is yet to respond to the video from Fedorov, whose dismissal sparked protests across the country .

During his tenure as defence minister, Fedorov was credited with energising the ministry, heading a drive against corruption and using data to analyse and try to improve performance on the front line.

His dismissal is widely accepted to have been related to tensions between him and army commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi. Syrskyi was also replaced several weeks later, after weeks of protests piled pressure onto the Ukrainian president.

Fedorov gave no indication as to his own political plans in the YouTube video, instead focusing on the need for a "legal, safe, and realistic mechanism that will allow Ukraine to restore a full democratic process even amidst a prolonged war".

He added that the country was facing a "systemic crisis of governance" and is "scared of change", and pointed to corruption in Ukraine as one of the things hurting the country's war effort.

Zelensky has since appointed Yevgeniy Khmara, a career intelligence official with a low political profile, as acting defence minister.

Other posts in Zelensky's government were offered to Fedorov, including deputy prime minister for military innovation, but the 35-year-old has said he would only return as defence minister.

A former minister of digital transformation, Fedorov set up a volunteer "IT Army of Ukraine" to launch cyber-attacks against Russians in the early days after its full-scale invasion.

Later, he led a successful fundraising campaign called the Army of Drones and brought in elements of "gamification" to the war, designing a system that awarded Ukrainian military units with credits for hitting Russian targets.

As defence minister, his focus on drones, high-tech warfare and procurement continued, and saw him ask SpaceX founder Elon Musk to stop Russia from using Starlink satellites for drone attacks.

The move has been credited with causing considerable disruption to Russia's frontline operations and advance.

title.en: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
title.zh: 在遭受干旱的法国，油轮提供饮用水

summary.en: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

Since early August, huge silver tanker trucks have been paying a visit to the town of Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines in Alsace, eastern France, twice a week. They aren't delivering heating oil or milk, but drinking water from the nearby town of Liepvre.

Sainte-Marie, with its population of 5,000, is located in a green valley in the Vosges Mountains and usually relies on about 20 mountain springs for its water. But the flow rate has fallen after weeks of intense heat and drought .

Liepvre, just a few kilometers away, is connected to a larger water supply network that extends toward the Alsatian plain. Here, there is still enough water despite the drought but because there is no permanent connection between the two systems, tanker trucks are effectively functioning as a water pipeline on wheels.

According to the French government, more than 40,000 people have been affected by water cutoffs or supply disruptions this month, and 550,000 are at higher risk of losing stable access.

The drought has affected large parts of France and water restrictions have been put in place in many regions, but tanker trucks are only being used in certain areas. This depends on what sources or groundwater reserves a municipality relies on for water and whether it can easily switch to other resources.

More than a dozen municipalities in the Jura Mountains, further to the south in the department of Doubs, are also currently being supplied by tanker trucks.

This situation is not new for France . In the summer of 2022, which was also exceptionally dry, tanker trucks were used to supply hundreds of municipalities with water. Others depended on bottled water.

Coucouron, a village in the Massif Central region of southern France with just under 800 residents, was severely affected .

Though it's located at a height of more than 1,000 meters (3,280 feet) in a region rich in water and where three major French rivers — the Loire, the Allier and the Ardeche, have their sources — an important spring ran dry after months of drought. Tanker trucks had to bring water to the villagers for months.

But drought wasn't the only reason for these problems. Experts discovered that there were several major leaks in the water supply network. Once they had been repaired, the village's water consumption dropped by about 40 cubic meters per day. A 6-kilometer-long (3.7-mile) pipeline linking to an additional water source is expected to bring more stability.

title.en: Trump pauses new tariffs on Canada and says countries close to a deal

summary.en: US President Donald Trump said he will delay imposing new tariffs on a wide array of Canadian goods for three days as the countries firm up a trade deal.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump said he will delay imposing new tariffs on a wide array of Canadian goods for three days as the countries firm up a trade deal.

"I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for a three day period, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalization of documents, have a DEAL!" Trump said in a social media post.

The announcement came less than two hours before a 50% levy on nearly $20bn (C$28bn) of Canadian imports were set to go in place.

The two sides have been at an impasse on several issues, including US tariffs on autos and many Canadian provinces banning American liquor sales.

Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke twice this week, and trade negotiators have been engaged in intense talks since July, after the US president threatened the new levy with a deadline of 19 August.

"Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done," Carney said in a letter posted on X.

In his post, Trump also said a final trade deal could allow the revival of the Keystone XL pipeline. The oil pipeline, which would connect Alberta to the US, was blocked by both the Obama and Biden administrations.

Environmentalists and indigenous groups have long opposed the pipeline but Trump has said multiple times he would like to revive the project, which would carry 830,000 barrels of oil a day.

"The great Keystone XL Pipeline, long ago killed by Sleepy Joe Biden, may be awoken from the grave!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"The deal will include comprehensive market access for all American goods, economic security commitments, digital trade alignment", US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer's office posted on X.

It will also include "many important provisions that will continue to protect our market and American workers, along with our Canadian partners", it added.

The extension is welcome news for Canadian negotiators and for businesses on both sides of the border, who have warned that the new tariffs would be harmful to both countries.

Tensions have mounted between the two major trading partners since Trump returned to office in January last year and he unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs, upending decades of free trade between Canada and the US.

The latest tariffs threatened by Trump were to be applied on a range of Canadian imports, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.

They would have been in addition to existing tariffs the US had already imposed on Canadian steel and aluminium, autos and lumber.

Canada has been in pursuit of a deal that would have the US drop or reduce tariffs on these key sectors.

The US, meanwhile, has been asking for a number of concessions from Canada,...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，随着两国敲定贸易协议，他将推迟三天对多种加拿大商品征收新关税。 “我已暂停对加拿大征收 50% 的关税，该关税原定于明天早上开始实施，为期三天，因为加拿大和美国在文件最终确定后达成了协议！”特朗普在社交媒体帖子中说道。 该公告是在对加拿大近 200 亿美元（合 280 亿加元）进口商品征收 50% 关税之前不到两小时宣布的。 两国在多个问题上陷入僵局，包括美国对汽车征收关税以及加拿大许多省份禁止销售美国酒类。 特朗普和加拿大总理马克·卡尼本周两次发表讲话，自 7 月以来，在美国总统威胁以 8 月 19 日为最后期限征收新税之后，贸易谈判代表一直在进行激烈的谈判。 卡尼在 X 上发布的一封信中表示：“尽管仍有重要工作要做，但已经取得了实质性进展。” 特朗普在帖子中还表示，最终贸易协议可能会让 Keystone XL 管道复兴。连接阿尔伯塔省和美国的石油管道被奥巴马和拜登政府封锁。 环保主义者和土著团体长期以来一直反对该管道，但特朗普多次表示他希望恢复该项目，该项目每天将输送 83 万桶石油。 “伟大的基斯通XL管道，很久以前就被瞌睡乔·拜登杀死了，现在可能会从坟墓里醒来！”特朗普在《真相社会》上撰文。 美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔办公室在 X 上发布消息称，“该协议将包括所有美国商品的全面市场准入、经济安全承诺、数字贸易协调”。 它还将包括“许多重要条款，将继续保护我们的市场和美国工人以及我们的加拿大合作伙伴”，它补充说。 对于加拿大谈判代表和边境两侧的企业来说，延期是一个受欢迎的消息，他们警告说新关税将对两国都有害。 自特朗普去年1月重返办公室并推出广泛的全球关税计划以来，这两个主要贸易伙伴之间的紧张关系不断升级，颠覆了加拿大和美国之间数十年的自由贸易。 特朗普威胁对一系列加拿大进口产品征收最新关税，包括葡萄酒、乳制品、水泥、服装和曲棍球设备。 这些关税是在美国已经对加拿大钢铁、铝、汽车和木材征收的现有关税之外附加的。 加拿大一直在寻求一项协议，让美国放弃或减少对这些关键行业的关税。 与此同时，美国一直要求加拿大做出一些让步……

title.en: South Korea shortens war games with US, citing Washington request
title.zh: 韩国援引华盛顿要求缩短与美国的军演

summary.en: It comes after Trump announced plans to curtail joint military exercises with South Korea, citing a "very good" relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
South Korea's annual joint military drills with the US will be cut short by six days at the request of Washington, its defence ministry has announced.

Seoul said that the "period and scale" of the 2026 Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise had been adjusted due to a "proposal of the US side".

The drill will now conclude on 21 August, rather than 27 August as planned. It comes after Donald Trump announced plans to curtail exercises with South Korea, citing his "very good" relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.

South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun told a parliamentary hearing that neither South Korean nor US officials had been aware in advance about Trump's plans.

The combined field training exercise component of the drills will also be "partially reduced in scale", Seoul said, noting that the "specific details" of that reduction are still under discussion.

The announcement comes after US officials told the Wall Street Journal that Trump is pushing his aides for a meeting with Kim Jong Un.

Sources told the outlet that the US president had privately discussed setting up an in-person discussion with Kim during his next trip to Asia, which will likely be in November for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation in China.

Over the weekend, Trump wrote on Truth Social: "These exercises are not only costly, with much of these costs paid for by the United States of America (as usual!), but send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile."

He added: "While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, 'No thanks!'"

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Monday, the president again explicitly linked his decision to South Korea's refusal to "give us a little hand" with Iran.

"We have 39,000 soldiers over there guarding you from Kim Jong Un, your next door neighbour, and you're not going to help us on a very easy military operation in Iran," he said. "That's strange".

US and South Korean military leaders announced the Ulchi Freedom shield in a joint press conference last week.

At the time, they said the event would be similar in scale to previous years, with about 18,000 South Korean soldiers participating. About 28,500 American military personnel are stationed in South Korea.

During the news conference, military leaders also mentioned North Korea's deployment of troops to aid Russia's war against Ukraine.

US military spokesperson Ryan Donald said "our training accounts for that threat", referring to North Korean soldiers returning from the battlefield.

Following that press conference, North Korea's foreign ministry condemned the joint military drills as "a rehearsal for an aggressive war".
body.zh: 韩国国防部宣布，应华盛顿的要求，韩国与美国的年度联合军事演习将缩短六天。 首尔表示，由于“美方的提议”，2026年乙支自由之盾演习的“期限和规模”已进行调整。 演习现将于8月21日结束，而不是原计划的8月27日。此前，唐纳德·特朗普宣布计划减少与韩国的演习，理由是他与朝鲜金正恩的关系“非常好”。 韩国外交部长赵贤在议会听证会上表示，韩国和美国官员事先都不知道特朗普的计划。 首尔表示，演习中的联合野战训练演习部分也将“部分缩减规模”，并指出缩减的“具体细节”仍在讨论中。 此前，美国官员告诉《华尔街日报》，特朗普正在敦促其助手与金正恩会面。 消息人士告诉媒体，美国总统曾私下讨论过在下一次亚洲之行期间与金正恩进行面对面的讨论，这次访问很可能是在 11 月份在中国举行的亚太经济合作组织会议上。 周末，特朗普在《Truth Social》上写道：“这些演习不仅成本高昂，其中大部分费用由美利坚合众国支付（像往常一样！），而且还发出了完全不恰当和充满敌意的信号。” 他补充道：“虽然有些无关（？），但我最近问韩国总统他们是否愿意加入我们的伊朗伊斯兰共和国无核化进程，他们说，‘不，谢谢！’” 总统周一在椭圆形办公室对记者发表讲话时，再次明确地将他的决定与韩国拒绝在伊朗问题上“帮助我们”联系起来。 他说：“我们有 39,000 名士兵在那里保护你们免受邻国金正恩的伤害，你们不会帮助我们在伊朗进行一次非常轻松的军事行动。” “这很奇怪”。 美国和韩国军方领导人在上周的联合新闻发布会上宣布了乙支自由之盾。 当时，他们表示此次活动的规模与往年相似，约有18000名韩国士兵参加。大约有28,500名美国军事人员驻扎在韩国。 在新闻发布会上，军方领导人还提到朝鲜部署军队援助俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争。 美国军方发言人瑞安·唐纳德表示，“我们的训练说明了这一威胁”，指的是从战场返回的朝鲜士兵。 在那次新闻发布会之后，朝鲜外交部谴责联合军演是“侵略战争的预演”。

title.en: Five Australian rules footy players suspended amid police investigation
title.zh: 五名澳式足球运动员在警方调查中被停赛

summary.en: The suspensions, for drinking and inviting women to a hotel, come as police investigate an alleged sexual assault.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Five players in the Australian Football League (AFL) have been banned for late-night drinking and inviting women to a hotel after a weekend match in Melbourne.

The Sydney Swans' Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice have been stood down from Australian Rules football's top league for the rest of the season, the club announced.

The suspension comes after detectives in Melbourne began an investigation into an alleged sexual assault, said to have to taken place in the early hours of Monday morning at the Pullman Hotel where the players were staying after the match.

Sydney Swans chairman Andrew Pridham apologised to fans, players and the wider community on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters, he explained that the sanctions were handed down because the players had breached the club's standards by drinking alcohol later than accepted and bringing women to the hotel.

In a statement published earlier in the day announcing the suspensions, the club said: "We respect there is an ongoing investigation by Victoria Police and the actions we have taken today are independent of this.

Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich told a media conference: "We're deeply embarrassed and ashamed that the poor choices of five of our players, and the impact that's had on the women involved and also the club.

He declined to say whether any of the players had been drug tested, saying that any testing would form part of the police inquiry.

A spokesperson for Victoria Police said officers have spoken to several people who were at the Pullman Hotel, but no one was formally interviewed or arrested.

On Tuesday, club officials held talks with the players ahead of their suspension.

AFL chief executive Andrew Dillon has described the reports of the alleged sexual assault as "deeply concerning".

Sydney has dominated this season, currently placing second on the ladder which guarantees them a spot in the qualifying and elimination finals' round that begins in two weeks.

The club is scheduled to play against North Melbourne at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Sunday, which will be the last fixture ahead of the finals.

Unlike some other Australian sports, the AFL does not have a strict no-fault stand-down policy on players charged with serious offences such as sexual assault, and instead handles cases on a discretionary and case-by-case basis.
body.zh: 澳大利亚橄榄球联盟（AFL）的五名球员因在墨尔本周末比赛后深夜饮酒并邀请女性到酒店而被禁止。 悉尼天鹅队宣布，悉尼天鹅队的艾萨克·希尼、查德·华纳、尼克·布莱基、詹姆斯·乔丹和莱利·比斯在本赛季余下的比赛中将不再参加澳式足球顶级联赛。 停赛之前，墨尔本的侦探开始对涉嫌性侵犯的事件进行调查，据称这起事件发生在周一凌晨，球员们赛后下榻的铂尔曼酒店。 悉尼天鹅队主席安德鲁·普里德汉姆周三向球迷、球员和更广泛的社区道歉。 他在接受记者采访时解释说，之所以实施制裁，是因为球员们违反了俱乐部的标准，他们在规定的时间内饮酒，并带女性进入酒店。 在当天早些时候宣布停赛的声明中，俱乐部表示：“我们尊重维多利亚警方正在进行的调查，我们今天采取的行动与此无关。 天鹅队首席执行官马修·帕夫利希在媒体发布会上表示：“我们对五名球员的糟糕选择以及对相关女性和俱乐部产生的影响深感尴尬和羞愧。 他拒绝透露是否有任何球员接受过药物测试，并表示任何测试都将成为警方调查的一部分。 维多利亚警方发言人表示，警方已经与铂尔曼酒店的几名人士进行了交谈，但没有人受到正式约谈或逮捕。 周二，俱乐部官员在停赛前与球员进行了会谈。 AFL 首席执行官安德鲁·狄龙 (Andrew Dillon) 称有关性侵犯的报道“令人深感担忧”。 悉尼队本赛季占据主导地位，目前在积分榜上排名第二，这保证了他们在两周后开始的预选赛和淘汰赛决赛中获得一席之地。 该俱乐部定于周日在悉尼板球场对阵北墨尔本，这将是决赛前的最后一场比赛。 与澳大利亚其他一些体育运动不同，澳大利亚橄榄球联盟对于被指控犯有性侵犯等严重罪行的球员没有严格的无过错停赛政策，而是根据具体情况酌情处理案件。

title.en: Iranian academic writes of US detention 'hell' over link to 1979 hostage crisis
title.zh: 伊朗学者撰文讲述因与1979年人质危机有关联而在美国被拘留的“地狱”经历

summary.en: An Iranian academic reported being held in US detention after her immigration status was revoked. The decision was reportedly linked to her husband being the son of a prominent figure involved in the 1979 hostage crisis.
summary.zh: 一名伊朗学者报告称，她在其移民身份被撤销后被美国拘留。据报道，这一决定与她的丈夫是1979年人质危机中一位重要人物的儿子有关。

body.en:
An Iranian woman detained for months in Texas has accused the US government of "bloodline punishment" after it revoked her family's green cards over her husband's ties to a prominent figure in Iran.

Maryam Tahmasebi, a professor of psychology and statistics in Los Angeles, her husband, Seyed Eissa Hashemi, and their teenage son - all permanent residents of the US - were detained by immigration agents in April.

Her husband's mother was a spokesperson for the group that took dozens of Americans captive during the 1979 Iran hostage crisis.

The State department has cited those ties as the reason for revoking the family's status.

Tahmasebi and her son remain at a detention centre in Dilley, Texas, while her husband endures "horrible conditions" at a separate South Texas Detention Facility in Pearsall, she wrote in The Nation magazine , external .

"We have been put through hell for the past four months, and our physical and mental health have deteriorated in ways that might not be reversible for years," Tahmasebi wrote.

Tahmasebi wrote her account from inside her detention facility, where she has limited access to email, according to Jack Mirkinson, a senior editor at The Nation.

Hashemi is the son of Masoumeh Ebtekar, who became known as "Screaming Mary" or "Sister Mary" for her English-language statements on behalf of the students who occupied the US embassy in Iran and held 52 Americans hostage for 444 days.

Ebtekar later went on to hold several Iranian government roles. She was most recently vice president for women and family affairs, but has not held a government role since 2021.

"The government had decided to punish my husband for being the son of a woman who was a translator for the Iranian hostage takers in 1979, before Eissa was even born," Tahmasebi wrote.

"I came here because I wanted to build a life for myself and my family that was defined by my own actions, not anyone else's," she wrote. "But now our lives are being upended for something someone else did nearly 50 years ago."

The US decision to revoke the family's status came amid several enforcement actions taken against relatives of regime officials, as US hostilities with Iran escalated this year.

At the same time, amid Iran's brutal crackdown on protesters months ago, some diaspora activists identified relatives of Iranian officials abroad and campaigned to revoke their legal status.

An online petition in January 2026 called for Hashemi's deportation from the US due to his mother's involvement in the hostage crisis. A few conservative US outlets carried reports from outside Hashemi's residence in the US in April.

Less than a week later, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the US would revoke the family's status.

title.en: US: Meta hooked children, prosecutors say, as trial over social media harm begins
title.zh: 美国：检察官称，社交媒体伤害案审判开始后，Meta 迷上了儿童

Four US states have taken Meta to court, accusing the social media giant of deliberately making Facebook and Instagram addictive for children. Meta has denied the charges.

Meta intentionally hooked and exploited children, a US federal court heard Tuesday   as a   landmark trial seeking to hold Meta accountable for the alleged harm its social media platforms cause children began in California.

Four US states, California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey, argue the company misled the public about the safety of Instagram and Facebook and deliberately made the apps addictive for minors.

Lawyers for the states also allege Meta  is violating privacy laws  by routinely collecting data on children under 13 without their parents' consent.

The states are seeking around $200 billion (€173 billion) in damages as well as significant changes to Meta's core platforms.

They are part of a coalition of 29 states that sued the tech giant in 2023 for allegedly building addictive features into its apps.

On Tuesday, opening statements were made in the federal court in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco.

Megan O'Neill, a deputy attorney general for California, laid out the case to the eight-person jury.

"You're going to hear that Meta knew a lot about kids' brains," O'Neill said. "This includes how they are constantly seeking rewards, how they are sensitive to social feedback and how they are still developing their ability to control impulses the way adults do."

O'Neill said that Meta had researched these vulnerabilities and talked about how its Instagram platform could be changed to respond to them.

She told the court of a Meta study titled 'The young ones are the best ones,' alleging that for the company, "kids are the product."

Meta attorney Paul Schmidt said in his opening statement that there was "no dispute" that some social media users face ​struggles. However, he said that research showed no ‌clear association between adolescents' social media use and their well-being.

Schmidt said that Meta had "tried to come up with tools" to help users who have negative experiences on its apps.

"Much of this lawsuit is about the government attorneys and their witnesses saying, 'in trying to improve, we'd do it a little differently,'" Schmidt said.

He argued that Meta's efforts to improve tools to help users on their platforms had been  "meaningful."

Former Meta employee and expert witness Arturo Bejar testified on Tuesday, despite the company's efforts to block his appearance at the trial.

title.en: German Africa Prize goes to Kenyan social entrepreneur
title.zh: 德国非洲奖授予肯尼亚社会企业家

summary.en: Wawira Njiru organizes meals for hundreds of thousands of schoolchildren in Kenya, while at the same time supporting local farmers. For this, she is being honored by the German Africa Foundation.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Wawira Njiru organizes meals for hundreds of thousands of schoolchildren in Kenya, while at the same time supporting local farmers. For this, she is being honored by the German Africa Foundation.

The German Africa Foundation (DAS) is presenting the German Africa Prize  to Wawira Njiru — a woman whose initiative has transformed schools meals throughout Kenya .

In the beginning, Njiru started by feeding a regular meal to 25 schoolchildren; at that time, she was only a student with a dream to scale up her operation and provide a daily meal to 100 children.

Today, her work reaches more than 660,000 children at over 1,900 schools across Kenya.

Through her social enterprise, Food4Education (F4E), Njiru has "transformed a charitable idea into a functioning school-feeding system that reaches children, engages families, and strengthens local economic cycles," said Claus Stäcker, chair of the independent Africa Prize jury and director ofprograms for Africa at Deutsche Welle (DW), which serves as the media partner of the annual event.

Stäcker referred to the F4E approach as "an African solution to a global problem," adding that in honoring her out of "dozens of outstanding individuals," the German Africa Foundation jury had "once again recognized an extraordinary young woman, who tenaciously pursues her dreams and convictions, serving as an example for thousands of committed and innovative Africans."

School meals in Kenya typically rely on a combination of funding: Parents cover part of the costs, which are supplemented by donations and government funds.

With F4E, that model extends to including local sources: about 80% of the food distributed by the organization comes from small-scale farmers.

This way, school meals are freshly sourced — and farmers have a reliable market for selling their produce.

"For a long time, school meals were viewed as charity. We've proven that it's economic infrastructure," said 35-year-old Njiru.

Njiru told DW that receiving the award is a great source of encouragement for her work, which over the years has taken a great deal of dedication and perseverance.

"I'm stubborn. Once I figure I want something, I try and work towards it. And, you know, it's hard to tell me something is not possible", she explained.

Through her organization — which now also assists other governments in planning similar programs — she said she has found a solution tailored to African realities.

DAS is a nonpartisan foundation dedicated to promoting a nuanced view of Africa in political circles and among the German public.

title.zh: 特朗普称未计划与伊朗谈判，并分享地图将霍尔木兹海峡标为“美国新领土”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump stated that no talks with Iran are planned, while also sharing a map that depicted the Strait of Hormuz as "new US territory." Iran has maintained its stance that it will not reopen the vital waterway unless the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，目前没有与伊朗进行谈判的计划，同时他还分享了一张地图，将霍尔木兹海峡标注为“美国新领土”。伊朗坚称，除非美国解除对伊朗港口的封锁，否则不会重新开放这条重要的航道。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has said no talks with Iran are underway and none are scheduled, as he posted a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as a new US territory.

Trump has been pressing his threat to claim sovereignty over the crucial energy waterway as the nearly six-month-old Iran war grinds on with little sign of resolution.

Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner had said on Monday that the US and Iran were having "very positive and active conversations", but the president denied that was the case.

"There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect," Trump wrote on his Truth Social network on Tuesday night.

"The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated."

US sources told the Agence-France Presse news agency there had been "positive" discussions with the Iranians, but added that Trump had decided to wait and asked his team not to engage until Iran was ready to make a deal.

In recent weeks, there has been a lull in fighting, though the United Arab Emirates has recently accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles — which landed at sea — targeting "maritime navigation." Iran, however, denied firing a missile toward the UAE.

Soon after, the UAE announced that "in light of regional escalations" it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran.

The UAE bore the brunt of Iranian missile and drone attacks in the first period of the war, but had not reported any attacks since the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that was meant to halt the fighting.

Earlier on Tuesday, Trump posted a map on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz as a "NEW U.S. Territory".

Iran has effectively shut down the chokepoint , through which a fifth of the world's oil would usually transit, in retaliation for the war launched by the US and Israel in late February.

Trump revisited the idea again earlier in the week in comments to reporters in the Oval Office.

This is not the first time that Trump, faced with a foreign policy obstacle, has threatened to annex foreign territory.

Since returning to power in 2025, he has threatened to make Canada the 51st US state, seize Greenland and Cuba, and has even alluded to taking control of the Gaza Strip, without following through on any of these threats.

Before the Iran war erupted on 28 February, the Strait of Hormuz was an open waterway with free passage.

reflection.en: In a world where tensions rise and diplomatic paths seem closed, the call to be peacemakers remains vital. title.en: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
title.zh: 独居休达街头的未成年人面临虐待风险

summary.en: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.

It's 8 a.m. at the Tarajal industrial park in the autonomous city of Ceuta. But there are no workers and truck drivers to be seen near the warehouses today. Instead, there are makeshift tents, some of them made out of cardboard, with mainly children and teenagers sleeping under dirty blankets.

According to certain estimates, there could be between 3,000 and 5,000 unaccompanied minors in Ceuta. Some are living on the streets because they cannot find a spot in one of the already overcrowded reception facilities in the enclave.

Amina (not her real name), a 14-year-old Moroccan girl, and her brother were among the 80,000 people who crossed the border into Spain from Morocco in late July. Though most of these have since left Ceuta , some 9,000 remain, according to the local authorities — and many are minors. "

What's worst is that we don't have toilets," said Amina. "We have to go somewhere in the bushes, but I don't dare go alone."

Close by is a Moroccan woman called Malika (also not her real name) who has spread out several blankets for herself and her four children. She told DW she was not making enough as a cleaning lady in Morocco , adding that she earned the equivalent of €7 ($8) per day.

"That's just not enough to provide for everyone," she said. "School will start again soon, and I don't have any money for books, nor even decent clothes for the children."

That's why she decided to take part in the mass crossing of the Spanish border last month when she read about it on social media. But now she doesn't know what to do.

"One child got sick. He had a high fever, but I couldn't get help anywhere," she said. In the end, she made compresses with water and vinegar to see if that would help.

But now she is particularly worried about her 12-and 14-year-old daughters, because the number of sexual assaults has risen sharply in the past week. Police are currently investigating at least 15 suspected cases of rape. The local authorities suspect the actual number of cases to be much higher.

Susana Ascaso, an emergency doctor at Ceuta University Hospital, said she had treated several young girls in recent days.

"Just yesterday, another 12-year-old came to the emergency room," she said. "She said that other migrants had harassed her and touched her inappropriately. She arrived here completely terrified and in tears. She was with a woman who had found her on the street. That woman saved the girl."

body.zh: 数千名无人陪伴的未成年人聚集在非洲北海岸的西班牙飞地休达。疾病和虐待盛行，当局承认他们不知所措。 上午 8 点，位于休达自治市的塔拉哈尔工业园区。但今天仓库附近没有看到工人和卡车司机。相反，有临时帐篷，其中一些是用纸板制成的，主要是儿童和青少年睡在肮脏的毯子下。 据估计，休达可能有 3,000 至 5,000 名无人陪伴的未成年人。有些人流落街头，因为他们在飞地已经人满为患的接待设施中找不到一席之地。 阿米娜（化名）是一名 14 岁的摩洛哥女孩，她和她的兄弟是 7 月底从摩洛哥越过边境进入西班牙的 8 万人中的一员。据当地政府称，尽管其中大多数人已经离开休达，但仍有约 9,000 人留下，其中许多人是未成年人。 ” 最糟糕的是我们没有厕所，”阿米娜说。 “我们必须去灌木丛里的某个地方，但我不敢一个人去。” 附近是一位名叫马利卡（Malika）（也不是她的真名）的摩洛哥妇女，她为自己和四个孩子铺好了几条毯子。她告诉德国之声，她在摩洛哥做清洁工赚的钱不够多，并补充说她每天的收入相当于 7 欧元（8 美元）。 “这还不足以养活所有人，”她说。 “学校马上就要开学了，我没有钱买书，甚至没有钱给孩子们穿像样的衣服。” 这就是为什么她上个月在社交媒体上看到有关大规模穿越西班牙边境的报道后决定参加这一活动。但现在她不知道该怎么办。 “一个孩子生病了。他发高烧，但我无法在任何地方获得帮助，”她说。最后，她用水和醋做了敷布，看看是否有帮助。 但现在她特别担心自己12岁和14岁的女儿，因为过去一周性侵犯的数量急剧上升。警方目前正在调查至少15起疑似强奸案。地方当局怀疑实际病例数要高得多。 休达大学医院的急诊医生苏珊娜·阿斯卡索说，她最近几天治疗了几名年轻女孩。 “就在昨天，另一名 12 岁的孩子来到急诊室，”她说。 “她说其他移民骚扰了她，并对她进行了不恰当的触摸。她到达这里时非常害怕，流着泪。她和一名在街上发现她的妇女在一起。那个妇女救了这个女孩。” 阿斯卡索表示，对于“18 岁以下的女孩”来说，情况尤其困难，她们“尤其面临风险”。她补充说，存在着严重的不平衡……

title.en: Designed to 'exploit' children: Meta faces a historic courtroom reckoning
title.zh: 旨在“剥削”儿童：Meta 面临历史性的法庭清算

summary.en: The trial's outcome could help reshape Facebook and Instagram, and leave Meta with billions of dollars to pay in penalties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Meta knowingly hooked and exploited children, a United States federal court has heard in the trial of the social media giant on charges that it deliberately made Instagram and Facebook addictive to young users.

In what many experts have called social media's "big tobacco moment," a coalition of US states is demanding Meta pay US$200 billion ($282 billion) in penalties for using technology specifically designed to foster addiction among children in a similar fashion to cigarettes.

Meta "exploited how kids' brains work," California prosecutor Megan O'Neill said in opening arguments, painting Meta's business model as one built to "hook the users, hold them for as long as they can, harvest their data, and then hide the truth from the public".

"It worked especially well for kids," O'Neill added. "Meta needed kids, and it needed to reassure the people who cared about those kids that the kids are safe."

Meta's lawyer, Paul Schmidt, acknowledged that some users were harmed by the networks, but argued that the company had "tried to come up with tools to help them". He argued research showed no clear link between adolescents' social media use and a lack of well-being.

He also said Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's co-founder and CEO, shared the company's desire to improve its services, and not make them dangerous.

"They don't believe they're going to do well if people don't like their service," Schmidt said.

Before the trial began, the company denied all the allegations, insisting it had worked with parents, experts and law enforcement to incorporate protective safeguards for children.

This is not the first case seeking to hold tech companies — including Meta — accountable for these types of issues, but it could become one of the most consequential if it leads to sweeping changes on the platforms.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify, along with Instagram head Adam Mosseri.

Activists, including mothers of children they say were driven to suicide by their social media usage, rallied outside court.

One mother, Lori Schott, called out Zuckerberg and Mosseri, saying they "built one of those most powerful and richest companies in the world... But power does not excuse harm."

This is the first federal trial in what is expected to be a tidal wave of lawsuits also targeting TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube as families, educators and state governments charge them with harming the mental health of young people.

Meta, which has more than three billion users worldwide, is the sole defendant in this case.

title.en: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history leaves 2,300 dead in Congo
title.zh: 历史上增长最快的埃博拉疫情在刚果造成 2,300 人死亡

summary.en: The World Health Organization has said the current Ebola outbreak is on track to surpass the deadliest on record.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s fast-moving Ebola outbreak has now killed over 2,300 people and become the deadliest outbreak of the disease on record in the Central African nation.

The outbreak unfolding in one of DRC's most vulnerable regions is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever, with 4,945 cases including 2,325 deaths, according to government data.

It's the DRC's 17th outbreak, with a toll that has eclipsed that of the country's 2018-2020 outbreak when 2,299 deaths out of 3,481 cases were recorded.

The latest data shows 101 new cases and 33 deaths reported in the previous 24 hours. Over 1,000 people have recovered, while 730 remain in hospitals or isolation.

The outbreak has infected and killed more people at a greater speed than any other outbreak in history. The World Health Organization has said it is on track to surpass the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak in West Africa, the deadliest on record with more than 11,000 deaths.

Trish Newport, emergency coordinator with Doctors Without Borders, said the limited community engagement in the outbreak remains a key challenge.

"The community needs to be aware about the outbreak," she told The Associated Press news agency, adding that people "need to be involved in the response, and they need to know what the signs and symptoms are and what to do if they get sick. And this today is not happening in every single place where there are Ebola cases".

Starting from the first confirmed case, the outbreak reached 2,000 killed almost three times faster than in the 2014-16 outbreak.

Some families have lost up to 15 of their relatives in the epicentre, the Ituri province, Newport said.

"We rapidly need to scale up to be able to prevent more deaths from happening, more families and communities from being impacted," she added.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for the current outbreak across six provinces in Congo's east. Trials for those are ongoing in Ituri.

Most new cases and deaths are being reported outside of the people being monitored. Challenges facing medical teams dealing with the outbreak also include strikes by some unpaid health workers, threats by rebel groups, anger from long-traumatised communities, bad roads making it difficult to reach all the affected territories, and misinformation claiming that Ebola isn’t real.

title.en: Iran to go 'full offensive' if diplomacy fails as Trump threatens to bomb Oman
title.zh: 伊朗称若外交失败将“全面进攻”，此前特朗普威胁轰炸阿曼

summary.en: Iran has stated it will go on a "full offensive" if diplomatic efforts fail, following threats from the US to bomb Oman. Meanwhile, Iran has been negotiating an agreement with Oman regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz.

body.en:
Iran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to its war with the United States have stalled, as the US ruled out extending a temporary ceasefire agreement.

Progress towards peace talks and a resumption of oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz has ground to a halt, with no sign that the warring parties are moving towards ending the conflict that the US and Israel launched with attacks on Iran on 28 February.

"Iranian entities must be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and wider region, as Iran will be ready to make decisions and take action on difficult decisions," a senior Iranian official told Reuters news agency.

The official added that Iran would conduct a "timely and precise" military attack to break the US naval blockade if diplomacy failed.

Monday marked the day Iran and the US were expected to reach a final peace agreement under a memorandum of understanding signed in June aimed at ending the war.

Signed on 17 June, the MoU set a 60-day timeframe for the US and Iran to reach a broader deal on Iran's nuclear program and US sanctions.

The agreement, which declared the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts", quickly unravelled over a dispute about control of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the war.

Asked by reporters on Monday if the US was seeking to extend June's interim agreement, US President Donald Trump said no.

Iran said point 5 of the MoU gave it the right to manage the strait, which it shares with Oman, while the US rejected that interpretation. Hostilities resumed as Iran began firing on vessels it said were trying to sail through Hormuz on an unapproved route, and Trump said on 7 July that the pact was "over".

"Within the short period of a few weeks set by Iran, all the agreement's provisions must be implemented by the US. This is a precondition for further negotiations with the US," the Iranian official told Reuters, adding that mediators would share Iran's deadline with the US and regional countries.

Iran has been negotiating separately with its neighbour across the strait, Oman, to manage Hormuz, seen as a key component of a wider deal, and says it is close to an agreement, although progress has been slow.

Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way" of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz and called for Iran to surrender.

body.en:
Flags at government sites are flying at half-mast and security vehicles are parked in the heart of Beijing, as China mourns former Premier Zhu Rongji.

Zhu died of an illness last week at 97 and was cremated at a funeral in Beijing on Tuesday. The ceremony, attended by senior leaders including President Xi Jinping, was kept low-key. No footage has been released.

Zhu, who served as China's premier from 1998 to 2003, is remembered as one of the country's most important economic reformers.

While hailing the late premier as a "loyal" party member, the Chinese state is also wary that public mourning for his era of reform can easily turn into veiled criticisms of the current government under Xi.

Xi was among the leaders who had visited Zhu in hospital or sent condolences after his death, Chinese state media reported on Tuesday. Others included incumbent premier Li Qiang and ex-president Hu Jintao.

After his death, state media described Zhu as an "outstanding member of the Chinese Communist Party" and a "time-tested and loyal Communist fighter".

He was cremated at Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery, an exclusive resting place for high-ranking officials and other prominent figures.

Meanwhile, online, posts about Zhu have been contained and censored - including an essay written by economist Zhao Jian, which remembered Zhu's era as a time when people were "properly poor" but saw a clear future ahead.

"There were no smartphones then, no short-form videos and no screens filled by the purveyors of anxiety," he wrote.

"The sky was blue, life moved slowly and people could say what they really thought."

The party has long been fearful of public reaction to deaths of senior officials and public figures.

The deaths of former premier Zhou Enlai in 1976 and former CCP general secretary Hu Yaobang in 1989 prompted widespread outpourings of grief that morphed into protests.

Zhu died just days before the Communist Party leadership gathered to commemorate the birth centenary of President Jiang Zemin, who died in 2022.

The death of Zhu and Jiang, two prominent leaders from the same era, has prompted a wave of nostalgia among many Chinese people for a time when the country looked as if it was going in a different direction - when it appeared that it may open to the world and allow more freedom for its people.

Previously purged under Mao Zedong's regime, Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death in 1976.

Zhu served as premier alongside Jiang Zemin, who became Communist Party chief in 1989 and president in 1993.

The two men served alongside each other at the top of China's leadership from 1998 to 2003, leading China through an era of rapid economic growth and entry into global trade.

body.zh: 对母子电影“糟糕透了”的评论促使人们去电影院观看一部关于一头牛和云雀的粗糙、低科技动画在中国票房上取得了巨大成功，与《奥德赛》和《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》等大片并列影院收入排行榜。 《牛来》的意思是“牛来了”，这是一部 86 分钟的预算动画，讲述了新生小牛和云雀之间的关系在抽象梦境过程中发展的故事。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story reminds us that true worth and success are not always judged by conventional standards or initial human critique. Yahweh is the one who ultimately determines who rises and who falls, often surprising us with what He chooses to bless.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，真正的价值和成功并非总是由传统标准或最初的人类评论来评判。雅伟是最终决定谁兴盛谁衰落的那一位，祂常常以出人意料的方式赐福我们。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: China’s economy showing signs that slowdown may be extending
title.zh: 中国经济放缓迹象或将延长

summary.en: China's economy is experiencing an extended slowdown, with industrial output and retail sales declining in July. This follows one of the country's weakest quarterly growth rates and increases pressure on Beijing for intervention.
summary.zh: 中国经济显示出放缓可能正在加剧的迹象，7月份工业产出和零售额均出现下滑。此前，中国经历了有史以来最疲软的季度增长率之一，这给北京带来了干预的压力。

body.en: Industrial output and retail sales slump in July after one of the country’s weakest quarterly growth rates ever China’s economy is showing signs of extending a slowdown with a slump in industrial output and retail sales in July, adding to pressure on Beijing to intervene with measures to support activity. After the world’s second largest economy posted one of its lowest quarterly growth readings on record in the three months to June, the latest figures suggest it continued to falter in July. Continue reading...
body.zh: 继中国有史以来最弱的季度增长率之一之后，7 月份工业产出和零售销售大幅下滑。随着 7 月份工业产出和零售销售的下滑，中国经济显示出持续放缓的迹象，这加大了北京方面采取干预措施支持经济活动的压力。在这个世界第二大经济体公布了截至 6 月份的三个月以来有记录以来最低的季度增长数据之一后，最新数据显示该经济体 7 月份继续下滑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As a nation faces economic headwinds, it's natural to focus on policy and human intervention. Yet, this moment can also be a reminder that Yahweh is the ultimate source of our ability to create and sustain wealth. In times of plenty or scarcity, remembering His provision helps us anchor our hope beyond fluctuating markets.
reflection.zh: 当一个国家面临经济逆风时，人们自然会关注政策和人为干预。然而，这一刻也可以提醒我们，雅伟是我们创造和维持财富能力的最终来源。无论是在富足还是匮乏之时，记住祂的供应有助于我们将希望锚定在波动市场之外。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

"Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in...
body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. Indonesia's efforts to navigate its foreign policy amidst regional tensions reflect the ongoing challenge of living at peace with all, as far as it depends on them. This pursuit requires wisdom and a steadfast commitment to de-escalation and understanding.
reflection.zh: 在复杂的地缘政治格局中，各国常努力维持和平与中立。印度尼西亚在区域紧张局势中努力调整其外交政策，反映了在力所能及的范围内与所有人和平相处的持续挑战。这种追求需要智慧和对缓和局势、增进理解的坚定承诺。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: After Hormuz, China looks to the promise – and peril – of the Arctic’s ‘ice silk road’
title.zh: 继霍尔木兹海峡之后，中国着眼于北极“冰上丝绸之路”的机遇与风险

summary.en: China has initiated the first regular shipping transits through the Arctic's northern sea route, aiming to establish an "ice silk road." This new maritime path, however, raises significant concerns regarding its potential environmental impact and geopolitical implications.
summary.zh: 中国已开通北极航线的首次定期运输，旨在建立一条“冰上丝绸之路”。然而，这条新的海上航线在环境影响和地缘政治方面引发了重大担忧。

body.en: China has established the first scheduled transit through the northern sea route, but questions remain over the environmental and political risks When Marco Rubio suggested that the world should look to new shipping lanes to bypass the logjammed strait of Hormuz, it’s unlikely he had the Arctic’s northern sea route in mind. And yet in recent months the promise of this 5,500km channel – cleaved through frozen seas by nuclear-powered icebreakers and illuminated by a sun that never dips below the Arctic horizon – has grown. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中国已经建立了第一条通过北方海路的定期过境航线，但环境和政治风险仍然存在问题。当马可·卢比奥建议世界应该寻求新的航道以绕过堵塞的霍尔木兹海峡时，他不太可能想到北极的北方海路。然而近几个月来，这条 5,500 公里长的航道 — — 由核动力破冰船劈开冰冻的海洋，并由永远不会低于北极地平线的太阳照亮 — — 的前景越来越大。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The pursuit of new trade routes like the Arctic's "ice silk road" highlights humanity's drive for progress and efficiency. Yet, as the story notes, such ventures also carry significant environmental and political risks that demand careful consideration. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to foresee danger and take precautions, rather than rushing headlong into...
reflection.zh: 像北极“冰上丝绸之路”这样的新贸易路线的开辟，彰显了人类对进步和效率的追求。然而，正如报道所指出的，此类项目也伴随着重大的环境和政治风险，需要我们审慎考量。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们预见危险并采取预防措施，而不是为了短期利益而贸然陷入潜在的危机。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: A fake website and a deluge of CVs: the Australian firm embroiled in an FBI probe into alleged Chinese espionage
title.zh: 虚假网站与大量简历：澳大利亚公司卷入联邦调查局对涉嫌中国间谍活动的调查

summary.en: An Australian firm has been caught up in an FBI investigation into alleged Chinese espionage, involving a fake consultancy website that impersonated the Brisbane company. This fake site was among 13 websites seized by the US Department of Justice.
summary.zh: 一家澳大利亚公司卷入联邦调查局对涉嫌中国间谍活动的调查，其中涉及一个冒充这家布里斯班公司的虚假咨询网站。这个虚假网站是美国司法部查获的13个网站之一。

body.en: Exclusive: Fake consultancy impersonating Brisbane firm online is one of 13 websites seized by the US Department of Justice Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast When the first emails arrived, they were easily dismissed as spam. But as strangers continued to boast about their defence and security credentials, they became impossible to ignore. From mid-2025, a small Australian consultancy firm called Horizzen started receiving emails and strange calls from people applying for vague jobs in the United States. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：在线冒充布里斯班公司的虚假咨询公司是美国司法部查获的 13 个网站之一 关注我们的澳大利亚新闻直播博客以获取最新更新 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 当第一批电子邮件到达时，它们很容易被视为垃圾邮件而被忽略。但随着陌生人继续吹嘘他们的国防和安全资历，他们变得不可能被忽视。从 2025 年中期开始，一家名为 Horizzen 的澳大利亚小型咨询公司开始收到人们在美国申请模糊工作的电子邮件和奇怪的电话。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights how deception, even when elaborately crafted, often has a limited lifespan. While falsehoods may initially mislead, their true nature is eventually revealed, as seen in the seizure of these fake websites. Yahweh's word reminds us that truth ultimately prevails, and deceit cannot endure indefinitely.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻揭示了欺骗，即使精心策划，也往往寿命有限。虚假信息可能一时蒙蔽，但其真实面目终将被揭露，正如这些虚假网站被查获一样。雅伟的话语提醒我们，真理最终会得胜，谎言无法永远持续。

verse.textEn: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
verse.textZh: 口吐真言，永远坚立；舌说谎话，只存片时。

title.en: How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing
title.zh: 如何购买“巨型橡皮艇”：危险的英吉利海峡偷渡新模式

summary.en: The Guardian China reports on the alarming trend of large dinghies, capable of carrying hundreds, being used for perilous Channel crossings. The article investigates the supply chain for these vessels, noting that large orders are readily fulfilled by manufacturers.
summary.zh: 《卫报》中国版报道称，载有数百人的大型充气艇被用于危险的英吉利海峡偷渡，这一趋势令人担忧。文章调查了这些大型船只的来源，指出制造商可以轻松满足大批量订单。

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. Additional reporting by Lyndon Li Continue reading...
body.zh: 载有数百人的船只是一个明显且令人震惊的趋势。但这么大的船只从哪里来呢？他们表示，只要订单超过 20 艘，提供一艘在西欧波涛汹涌的海域使用的大型小艇就不成问题。这家中国公司的销售经理甚至还为一位冒充潜在客户的卫报卧底记者准备了一份在线手册供其细读。他们的生产能力为每月 500 艘船，是的，有可能以合适的价格获得更大的船。他们可以以每艘 1,678 美元（1,238 英镑）的价格制造一艘七米甚至八米长的军用小艇，不带发动机，但这将缺乏 CE 认证，这是表明产品符合欧盟健康和安全要求的强制性标志。林登·李的补充报道继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report on the supply of vessels for perilous journeys reminds us of the vulnerable individuals seeking safety and new beginnings. Yahweh calls us to recognize His presence in those who are marginalized and in desperate need. Our compassion for 'the least of these' reflects our love for Him.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于用于危险旅程的船只供应的报道，提醒我们那些寻求安全和新生活的弱势个体。雅伟呼召我们要在那些被边缘化和极度需要的人身上认出祂的存在。我们对“这些最小的弟兄”的怜悯，反映了我们对祂的爱。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: The Fauci hearing was painful to watch. But we need answers on Covid-19’s origin| David Relman
title.zh: 福奇听证会令人痛苦，但我们需要新冠病毒起源的答案 | 大卫·雷尔曼

summary.en: Despite recent congressional hearings, understanding the origin of Covid-19 remains elusive, with a microbiologist observing a deterioration in public discourse surrounding the issue.
summary.zh: 尽管近期国会举行了听证会，但了解新冠病毒的起源仍然困难重重，一位微生物学家指出，围绕这一问题的公共讨论正在恶化。

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. David Relman is a professor of medicine and microbiology at Stanford University. He was an inaugural member of the US National Science Advisory Board for Biosecurity and president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管最近在国会举行了听证会，但我们似乎距离了解 Covid-19 起源的目标比以往任何时候都更远。作为一名微生物学家和传染病临床医生，很难看到最近公众关于 Covid-19 起源的讨论的转移。对我来说，阅读安东尼·福奇在他现已公开的日记中关于起源争论的评论尤其困难。 7 月 29 日美国参议员兰德·保罗主持的电视节目对福奇进行敌意审讯，令人感到痛苦。尽管包括我自己在内的许多人早期呼吁对我们所知道、不知道和需要了解的 Covid-19 起源进行冷静、客观的评估，但我们现在似乎比以往任何时候都离这个目标更远——受到政治化、两极分化和不合逻辑思维的困扰。大卫·雷尔曼是斯坦福大学医学和微生物学教授。他是美国国家生物安全科学咨询委员会的首任成员和美国传染病学会主席继续阅读...

reflection.en: The struggle to understand complex issues like the origin of Covid-19, especially amidst contentious public discourse, reminds us of the wisdom in seeking thorough examination. Proverbs 18:17 suggests that true understanding emerges only after hearing all sides and carefully scrutinizing every claim. This calls for patience and a commitment to truth beyond...
reflection.zh: 在围绕新冠病毒起源等复杂问题展开的激烈公共讨论中，我们努力寻求理解，这提醒我们彻底审查的重要性。箴言18:17指出，真正的理解只有在听取各方意见并仔细审查每项主张之后才能浮现。这要求我们超越初步印象，以耐心和对真理的承诺，从而走向更清晰的道路。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Follow today’s news live Follow our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast ‘Collapsing confidence’ in housing market, Wilson says Tim Wilson has jumped on that reporting around rent increases and says there has been a collapse in confidence since the budget which is hurting renters. We’ve had, since the budget, collapsing confidence, a lack of will to invest in housing that is going to be available for rentals. body.en:
The leaders of Australia and Thailand have agreed to step up joint efforts to tackle transnational crime, while also pledging to elevate defence and trade ties.

Thailand prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in his first visit to Australia since he became leader in late 2025, met with his counterpart Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Wednesday.

The pair agreed to bolster mutual commitments to handle transnational crime, including tasking their law-enforcement agencies to "disrupt increasingly sophisticated global criminal networks", they said in a joint statement.

The nations will also elevate their security relationship by committing to a biannual meeting of defence ministers.

In a boost for Australia's fuel security, Albanese said his counterpart had made the "generous offer" of access to jet fuel, as energy markets experience supply-chain shocks as a result of the US-led war on Iran.

"Building on the strong economic ties is a top priority for my government," he told reporters.

"Times of uncertainty call for greater global cooperation between partners who are reliable and dependable, and friends."

In 2027, Australia and Thailand will mark 75 years since diplomatic relations were established between the two countries.

Anutin said: "I'm confident that our strategic partnership will remain an enduring foundation for Thailand and Australia ... and bring our countries and peoples even closer together."

"I extend my sincere appreciation once again to my dear Prime Minister Albanese and the Australian people for their warm hospitality."

The bid to crack down on transnational crime comes after Thailand tries to alleviate its reputation for being a hotspot for grey money — illicit capital that crosses borders.

The nation is an international hub for online scam work which fleeces millions of dollars from Australians each year.

Vulnerable Thai locals are often imprisoned by criminal syndicates on the outskirts of Bangkok to run the centres.

The Australian Federal Police was involved in a 2025 investigation that led to the arrest of five Australians, as well as United Kingdom, Canadian and South African nationals, operating a scam Bangkok "boiler room".

That announcement also came hours after Thai police confirmed the cause of death of a Thai woman allegedly murdered by an Australian man in June.

The Thai teenager, Tunchanok Donhomla, was allegedly suffocated, according to a police autopsy report seen by the ABC.

Thai police told ABC News that, on the basis of evidence collected, they now believed the investigation was reaching its completion.

title.en: Labor reveals super increase position amid 'predatory' practices crackdown

body.en:
Labor will not increase how much superannuation employers must pay workers, instead focusing on reforms to stamp out "predatory" practices used to lure people to put retirement savings into risky investments.

The superannuation guarantee rate — the minimum percentage of a worker's earnings that employers must pay into a retirement fund — is 12 per cent, and there have been calls within Labor to raise the rate to 15 per cent.

While rebuffing the need to increase the guarantee rate, the government is doubling down on its defence of the superannuation system amid calls from One Nation to allow workers to withdraw funds before retirement to help pay off mortgages.

"There's no plans to lift the super guarantee," Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino, who will unveil the long-awaited consumer protection reforms later on Wednesday, told ABC's Radio National.

He said raising the rate to 12 per cent was something Labor had long pushed for and that was now "putting people in a very strong position" for retirement.

Mulino will detail the long-awaited crackdown on predatory practices in an address to the National Press Club on Wednesday, after the high-profile collapses of First Guardian and Shield Master Funds in 2024 and 2025 stripped an estimated 12,000 Australians of their retirement savings.

One Nation has pushed to loosen rules around early access, while the government ruled out any rise to the compulsory super guarantee on Wednesday morning.

The reforms target "lead generators" — operators who use social media, online ads and cold calls to funnel people's retirement into high-risk schemes.

Unlicensed real-time communication about superannuation will be banned, and licensees will be required to take reasonable steps to ensure lead generation activities comply with legal requirements.

The anti‑hawking regime will also be bolstered, with stronger consent requirements, a narrower exemption for financial advisers to existing clients, and harsher penalties for breaches.

Mulino said the reforms were designed to strengthen consumer protections and disrupt "predatory and inappropriate behaviour" that led to the collapse of the Shield and First Guardian funds.

"Lead generators reaching out to these people in unsolicited ways, undertaking highly manipulative interactions to convince them that their super products were not performing well or were inappropriate, and then manipulating them into inappropriate products for them," Mulino told ABC radio on Wednesday morning.

The government previously floated the measures in a consultation paper published in April.

Sydney Swans chairman Andrew Pridham has apologised to the club's fans and corporate partners over the conduct of five players who have been stood down after the club found they had breached its standards on the night they were linked to a sexual assault investigation.

Pridham and Sydney Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich fronted media on Wednesday afternoon, hours after the club confirmed Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordon and Chad Warner would not be considered for selection for the remainder of the season, including the finals.

The sanctions follow an incident at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne that is being investigated by Victoria Police as an alleged sexual assault.

Five players were linked to the investigation and have not been arrested or charged.

He offered a "sincere apology to the community, to our many fans, our corporate partners, who've been amazingly supportive of us and understanding that we are attempting to deal with this matter as quickly as we can, as honestly as we can".

Pavlich said the club's AFLW team — who play a double-header alongside the men's side this weekend — were "deeply disappointed" by the incident and that "their welfare is of the utmost importance to us".

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Aussies have long held a narrative of the resilient "battler". But recent history suggests the days of "she'll be right" may be behind us. Insight explores whether the little Aussie battler still exists or whether a culture of complaint has taken over. Watch Insight episode Wired to Whinge on SBS On Demand.

My successes in the art of complaining have ranged from a $400 payment from my bank when they failed to get me a replacement transaction card before an overseas trip, to a payout for medical bills from an airline on behalf of a friend's mother who was injured on the plane.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Born in the 50s, I grew up mostly in Sydney's inner-west in a time when even an eye roll was perhaps considered subversive of the notion that we shouldn't complain too much.

Because of this, I was always terrified of being seen as a whinger and would bury any grievances I had about all the ways women were treated.

Then feminists such as Germaine Greer and Betty Friedan hit my consciousness at around age 15, and I realised how much women endured, which made me have newfound respect for my mum.

Despite this awareness, I continued for the next decade to put up with many experiences I believed were just typical for young women.

I didn't complain when I spent half a day getting ready for a date, and they'd show up looking like they just fell out of bed; I didn't complain when my bum was pinched as a barmaid or when I'd have to lock myself in a storeroom to avoid the advances of a coworker.

It wasn't until my mid-20s, working as a social worker, mostly in the criminal justice system, that I was surrounded by many women who taught me I didn't need to put up with it.

Then, when I was a 34-year-old mother of two, I earned my law degree and really felt empowered to complain, as it taught me how to navigate the systems and rules that structure society.

I thought, "I know the system. I know how it's supposed to work, so I'm not going to keep my mouth shut anymore."

As a social worker and solicitor, who also worked for the NSW Ombudsman, I've learnt a lot from other “professional complainers” over the past four decades — even if some seemed worn from battling bureaucracy and institutions.

My "professional complaining" has largely been advocating for others for housing and those experiencing addiction. People call me up with an issue they need help with, and they know I'll gladly open my big mouth and advocate for them, wasting no time to get their issues resolved.

I think people could complain more, but they don't know how to do it successfully; there is a process you must follow to be a good complainer.

body.en:
Many Australians want to go fully electric. But it’s often hard to know where to start. Solar? A home battery? Or quitting gas?

To find the best way to make the shift, we modelled three pathways for a three-bedroom house in Melbourne’s western suburbs.

These pathways show it’s important to do things in the right order. It’s best to start by lowering energy demand through better insulation and stopping draughts, and then switch from gas heating to an efficient reverse-cycle air conditioner. Home batteries should ideally be done last.

We used benchmark data to model a household with ducted gas heating, gas hot water and cooktop, common electric household appliances and a petrol car.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Each year this household uses 5,300 kilowatt-hours of electricity, just under 50 gigajoules of gas, and about 1,230 litres of petrol (to drive 11,100 kilometres). This costs $2,477 for electricity, $1,494 for gas and $2,255 for petrol. Total energy costs are $6,226 a year.

We modelled replacing these with a 10-kilowatt ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner, a hot water heat pump and an induction cooktop.

We also modelled two further options: one where the household switches to a mid-range EV with a battery of about 60kWh and another where the household keeps its petrol car.

We tested three pathways to going electric. These don’t include rebates or the cost of the EV.

Here, the household adds a large 11.76kW solar array, gets off gas and replaces its petrol car with an EV.

Although total electricity use rises, the grid electricity bill falls due to solar. The new electricity bill would be about $1,800. Because gas and petrol costs fall to zero, the household saves about $4,400 yearly.

This pathway mirrors the first, but adds a 13.5kWh home battery at the end. The power bill falls to about $950. Savings would be about $5,300.

Here, the household doubles storage to 27kWh. The power bill drops to about $600. It doesn’t reach zero due to low solar over some periods and annual supply charges. Annual savings: about $5,900.

These figures combine the prices in Victoria's official guide with advertised price benchmarks for installed appliances as of June 2026. The hot water heat pump is costed after an upfront discount. body.en:
Australia's migration agent watchdog has vowed to remove "fake agents" from the profession following multiple cases of unlawful immigration assistance.

The Office of the Migration Agents Registration Authority (OMARA) has sanctioned three registered migration agents in what the government described as an "ongoing crackdown".

Julian Hill, the assistant minister for citizenship, customs and multicultural affairs, said the government is strengthening immigration oversight.

"When people pay a migration agent they rightly expect a qualified person will do the work, not an untrained, unregistered fake agent," he said in a government statement on Tuesday.

"No one would put up with people borrowing registration numbers from doctors, lawyers or financial planners and neither should they when hiring a registered migration agent."

OMARA's monitoring team was established in October and "proactively monitored" 85 registered migration agents during 2025-26, identifying 43 instances of non-compliance and addressing them through education, engagement and regulatory action, according to the government statement.

"Alongside the Investigations team, which examines allegations of serious misconduct, OMARA sanctioned 28 registered migration agents in 2025-26," it added.

In three separate cases, registered migration agents permitted unregistered individuals to provide migration assistance under the agents' Migration Agent Registration Numbers (MARNs), a practice commonly referred to as "front agent" activity.

In the first case, an agent’s registration was cancelled after OMARA determined that hundreds of visa applications submitted through three business ImmiAccounts involved either undisclosed immigration assistance or assistance provided by staff who were not registered migration agents.

ImmiAccount is the Department of Home Affairs' online portal for lodging and managing visa and citizenship applications.

In the second case, an agent was suspended after acknowledging that his son, who was not a registered migration agent, had provided immigration assistance on the business's behalf.

The investigation also uncovered allegations that clients had received falsified departmental correspondence intended to give the impression that visa applications had been lodged when they had not.

In the third matter, an agent was suspended after knowingly permitting another business director to lodge visa applications using the agent’s MARN while the director worked towards becoming a registered migration agent.

body.en:
Can a political party whose past and current members have described LGBTQI+ people as having a "mental illness" be one of the "gayest parties" in Australia?

It's a question provoked by recent comments from One Nation members in the past week.

When asked about former WA One Nation candidate Parminder Singh's comments — first reported by the ABC, that gay people have a "mental illness" — federal MP Barnaby Joyce rejected them as "highly offensive".

But some of Australia's most prominent LGBTQI+ activists and equality campaigners say the party has more work to do in convincing the community it's truly living up to that title.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It's probably fair to say the community’s reaction has been a mixture of confusion and incredulity," Equality Australia legal director Heather Corkhill told SBS News.

"It's not every day you have politicians from the same party declaring both that being gay is a mental illness and that they are the gayest party in Australia, all in the space of a week."

Singh — who has since apologised for his comments — isn't the only one to have said members of the LGBTQI+ community have a "mental illness".

In comments first reported by The Guardian, One Nation WA senator Tyron Whitten said during a podcast interview segment about 'gender' in August last year that "there's male, there's female, and then there's mental illness".

"If you want to wear a dress, that's fine. I don't care. But ... they can't keep saying that, 'Hey kids, that's normal'," he added.

"You're going to be a boy or you're going to be a girl. And parents that are promoting this, I think that's child abuse."

Joyce is adamant the party is not a "pack of homophobes", describing that as a "vindictive trope" against One Nation.

"We're not here to glorify, we're not here to vilify. We're here for people to live their own life," he said on Tuesday.

Jordan McSwiney, a senior research fellow at the University of Canberra, says while One Nation may accept the existence of the community, it "certainly doesn't embrace this community".

McSwiney listed past positions, votes and policies of the party on LGBTQI+ issues, including Joyce and Hanson personally opposing same-sex marriage and abstaining from the 2017 parliamentary vote, the party's opposition to the now-abolished Safe Schools program, and what he described as its "anti-trans" politics, and "homophobic" remarks by current and former members.

body.en:
Dozens of eleventh-hour amendments to a controversial bill designed to claw back runaway disability spending have passed the upper house despite outcry from advocates.

Labor has been touting changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme, including sweeping new powers for the relevant minister and a cut in social funding, since April in a bid to save $37.8 billion by the end of the decade.

The changes passed the Senate on Tuesday night, with 28 in favour and 12 against.

But just hours before a final vote on the bill was due to take place, the government unveiled 63 changes in response to community concern.

Under one change, severely disabled Australians who require constant care will be able to appeal decisions made by the NDIS minister that affect their funding.

Participants can request a variation to their plan for specific sections, including assistance with daily living.

Community and social participation funding, which is set to be slashed despite its role in helping disabled people access friends, appointments and work, will remain ineligible for appeal.

The changes to the scheme would take away a lifeline for thousands of Australians, Greens disability spokesperson Jordon Steele-John said.

"Labor and the Liberals got together in a room, and they decided to strip us of our rights, regardless of our safety and dignity," said Steele-John, who lives with a disability.

Increased penalties for NDIS providers benefiting from kickbacks have been included in the changes, along with specific whistleblower protections.

"There will be tough new aggravated integrity offences, including obtaining funds by deception, providing false or misleading information for abuse of position as a participant's nominee, or for intentionally destroying records," NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister told reporters before the amendments were voted on.

The changes passed the upper house on Tuesday night with little debate, following a deal struck with the coalition for the removal of a so-called widow tax hidden in the federal government's budget reforms.

In exchange for closing the loophole, which would have caused divorcees and widows to lose negative gearing entitlements on investment properties, the opposition will support Labor's bill.

The conflation of the previously unrelated topics rendered disabled people a political football, Steele-John said.

body.zh: 尽管倡导者强烈抗议，一项旨在收回失控的残疾人支出的有争议法案的数十项最后一刻修正案已在上议院获得通过。 自4月份以来，工党一直在宣传对国家残疾保险计划进行改革，包括赋予相关部长新的权力以及削减社会资金，以期在本世纪末节省378亿澳元。 这些改变于周二晚上在参议院获得通过，28 票赞成，12 票反对。 但就在该法案最终投票前几个小时，政府公布了 63 项变更，以回应社区的担忧。 根据一项变更，需要持续护理的严重残疾澳大利亚人将能够对 NDIS 部长做出的影响其资助的决定提出上诉。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 参与者可以要求更改特定部分的计划，包括日常生活方面的帮助。 社区和社会参与资金尽管在帮助残疾人联系朋友、约会和工作方面发挥了作用，但仍将被削减，但仍将没有资格上诉。 绿党残疾事务发言人乔登·斯蒂尔-约翰表示，该计划的改变将夺走数千名澳大利亚人的生命线。 “工党和自由党聚集在一个房间里，他们决定剥夺我们的权利，不顾我们的安全和尊严，”身有残疾的斯蒂尔-约翰说。 变更中包括对受益于回扣的 NDIS 提供者的更严厉处罚，以及特定的举报人保护。 NDIS 部长珍妮·麦卡利斯特 (Jenny McAllister) 在修正案投票前对记者表示：“将会出现新的严厉的严重诚信犯罪，包括通过欺骗获取资金、滥用参与者提名人的职位提供虚假或误导性信息，或故意销毁记录。” 在与联盟达成取消隐藏在联邦政府预算改革中的所谓寡妇税的协议后，这些改革措施于周二晚在上议院获得通过，几乎没有引起任何争议。 作为堵住这一漏洞的交换条件，该漏洞可能会导致离婚者和寡妇失去投资房产的负扣税权利，反对党将支持工党的法案。 斯蒂尔-约翰说，以前不相关的话题的合并使残疾人成为了政治足球。 财长吉姆·查尔默斯 (Jim Chalmers) 几周前就宣布了工党堵住漏洞的计划，但政府不打算在 2026 年晚些时候将其提交给议会，对该法案草案的磋商要到周五才会结束。 随着 NDIS 法律陷入困境......
